assertions.name: dependent_rows_are_redundant_on_both_sides
assertions.source: Indicator (1 = both Delta_pn == Q_beta + m_e and m_n == m_p + Q_beta + m_e hold, on the prediction side AND the target side, to the dashboard's serialization granularity). Residuals are ~1e-10 MeV, i.e. the rounding of the stored 12-significant-figure strings — not physics.

description: Shows that 3 of the 5 failing rows on the per-observable 100x L2 dashboard are algebraically dependent on the other 2, in both the prediction and the comparison target (the neutron target is constructed as M_P + M_E + Q_BETA, not measured independently). With the m_p row separately shown to be a registry-vintage artifact, the five reported failures reduce to two independent ones: Q_beta and m_mu. Audit-only; re-scores nothing.

data.caveat: Redundant does not mean wrong to report — m_n in MeV is a useful number. It means the row is not an independent test, so L2 planning must not count it as a separate front. M_N_MEV_CODATA_DIRECT IS an independent neutron value; it is simply not what this dashboard scores against.
